messages:
ingest-sre: Observability alert — large spike in connection attempts to /v1/generate (18x baseline). SYN-heavy, many half-open TLS handshakes, source IPs mostly IPv6 across several /48s. Rate ~120k conn/min. WAF 5xxs up, request queueing increasing. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/conn-flood

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0320-02 — runbook: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/ddos-layer7. Pager duty: security-oncall notified.

Priya S: Thanks. Initial read — looks like connection-flood/probe behavior targeting our generative endpoints. Not seeing payloads that look like valid API calls, many short-lived TLS handshakes. Priorities: contain traffic at edge (rate limit/conn limit), push WAF rule to drop obvious probe patterns, notify customers if we expect degradation.

Alex R: I'm going to push a temporary connection-rate policy at the edge LB and a stricter WAF rule for /v1/generate. Plan: per-src conn limit 40/min with exponential backoff, drop incomplete TLS handshakes after 3s. Applying now.

Alex R: Deploy snippet applied to edge config:
```
route /v1/generate {
  conn_rate_limit: 40/min
  tls_handshake_threshold_ms: 3000
  penalty_window: 600s
}
```
Pushed to global edge in prod-edge-1/2/3.

Network Eng: I've engaged upstream DDoS mitigation with our provider (ticket #PROV-9876). They're enabling SYN/TLS SYN proxy for the affected prefixes and will monitor. If they recommend BGP diversion we'll coordinate.

ingest-sre: After config change metrics: connection attempts to /v1/generate down 72%, error rate returned to normal. CPU on model-hosts decreased. Still seeing smaller probes from some ASNs — will block at WAF.

Alex R: Added WAF rule to block requests with empty SNI + client_hello size < 200 bytes and UA matching known probe signatures. Rule ID: 8f3c-ddos-2026. Example rule (simplified):
```
if (sni == "" && client_hello_len < 200 && ua =~ /curl|bot|python/) {
  action: block
}
```
Applied in staging then prod.

Maria G: Support — any user-facing impact? We have a few customers on Dedicated reporting higher latencies earlier. Should we send a heads-up?

Support Lead: Please draft a short status note: "We detected anomalous traffic affecting some API requests; mitigations in place; latency restored for most customers. Working on post-incident analysis." I'll review and send.

Priya S: Good. Capture the list of blocked prefixes and WAF rule IDs for the postmortem. Also ensure audit logs (edge ACLs, WAF events) are exported to the security bucket and keyed with the incident ID. Confirm KMS key access logs are present so we can correlate any key access during the window.

ingest-sre: Confirmed: exported WAF logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2026-0320-02/ and enabled KMS key audit forwarding.

Sam T: No signs of customer data exfil. This looks volumetric/probing. We'll keep provider mitigation for 4 hours and then taper rules.

Priya S: Action items: 1) Postmortem ticket and timeline (Alex), 2) Add automated detection for SYN/TLS handshake anomalies (ingest-sre), 3) Harden per-route default conn_rate_policy (security/edge), 4) Customer comms template (Support Lead). Assign owners and ETA 48h for initial write-up.

Alex R: Created postmortem ticket PM-2026-0320-02 and assigned owners. I'll take the timeline and WAF rules. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

Support Lead: Drafted customer note, sending in 10m after legal review.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0320-02 status -> mitigated. Monitoring continues for 60m.

Network Eng: Provider confirms SYN proxy holding; will release when metrics stable for 30m.

ingest-sre: Leaving this thread open for follow-ups. Will attach final graphs to PM ticket.
